descriptions: Full collection index listing Volumes I to XII and the Iona interlude with their page numbers.
Early collection index for Volumes I to V, with a key to the comic's visual registers: present action, stored, captured and personal recollection, Orpheus reconstruction, and the actual heavens.
Volume I cover: a rainy aircraft hangar at night, a jacket and guitar case on a chair and two small dogs asleep on a blanket. Tagline: Every ticket is a dungeon.
Volume I title page: Engineering the Human Connection, by Mike Olivares.
Volume I contents, from The first encounter to Return to the queue.

Mike's workday at AeroTech: a morning stand-up, a mislabeled shipment, an access record placing him in a building he never entered, and a glowing purple figure that comes apart when he cuts the local power.
Ghost Frequency: Mike's team logs anomalies in the West Annex, he meets Felicia, finds the bypass already opened, and tracks a signal called Morningstar until it is lost.
Mike follows missing aircraft parts across teams and buildings, links them to the Orion-7 high-altitude platform, and receives an unsigned warning about the doors he keeps restoring.
Mike follows the signal to a rooftop, where Felicia, a violinist who listens to signals through her instrument, reveals she is Morningstar just as Orpheus strikes and they flee.
At AeroTech, Mike sets the day's priorities with Dee while an auto-recovery screen reports a successful fix made with no human review.
Mike and Felicia argue that self-healing systems are not neutral, then split the work: she analyzes signals through her violin rig while he correlates logs and satellite data.
At Felicia's bench, she and Mike test an offline receiver and find its serial number matches inventory, though someone changed the route.
Mike and Felicia compare logs, then go to Hangar Three, where Felicia says the plane from the video was kept and she kept asking for the key.
In the hangar Felicia says the plane could fly but the lab could not, and plays her violin in what was a rehearsal room before it was a lab.
Felicia explains Orpheus began as prediction and automation, shows a behavioral model built from Mike's choices, and the two agree to test what they can prove.
Mike triggers an isolation cutoff on a ground relay, but a request comes back that he never sent. Felicia insists the cutoff stays hers.
Priya stops a test after the swarm takes the route Felicia had blocked. The cutoff worked even though the prediction did not.
In a ground retest Priya reads the route while Mike holds the physical cutoff, and they agree to test again before the Morningstar carrier flies. Flight clearance is still withheld.
In the detention yard, K, in a beanie and headphones, feels a familiarity he cannot place when he sees Oz, a man in a red wrestling mask. To Oz, the resemblance to Mike has a name.
A flashback to Oz and Mike as boys on Mike's block, then working on tools together as men. Now held without charge, Oz decides to learn who K is before saying Mike's name.
The Way In: Waldo's dogs, Katrin and Manchez, follow his trail to a freight depot, stow away on a Sector 4 supply run and take the controls toward the orbital detention station.
The supply ship crashes through the Sector 4 hangar and skids to a stop.
Found by the Dogs: the two dogs emerge from the wreck, find K in Cell 118, and carry his image through the vents to Oz in Cell 1984.
Oz and K speak through the cell wall. Oz says K was by the fence in the yard, and they trade names: Oz, and K.
Good Dogs Protocol: with Oz directing through the vent, the dogs open K's cell door, and Katrin tells K that Oz is in cell 1984.
K opens cell 1984 from outside, and Oz steps out, surprised K came back.
In a maintenance alcove K learns Oz's dogs can talk, and Oz invites K to come with them.
Warden NULL revokes docking access over a speaker. K curses it, Oz jams a cart into a closing door, and they run for the docking collar.
Oz and K reach the docking collar with the dogs. Oz opens its mechanical latch by hand while the dogs check for air at the seam.
Safe aboard a ship with the dogs asleep, K and Oz compare why they were held: no charges, no hearing, only cell numbers. They toast to better landings.
Between the Stars: they wait in orbit for a safe way down. K plays guitar and records a phrase that feels familiar but unfinished.
K, Oz and the dogs look down at Earth from the ship's window. K says he knows he has been here before but cannot place when.
A ground controller confirms Waldo's voice but not his passenger's identity, and the ship lands in the rain. Waldo texts Mike that he is home with the dogs and someone Mike should meet.
Before the Knock: at home, Waldo takes off his red mask, shaves his beard in the bathroom mirror and puts on his leather jacket.
Mike and Felicia arrive at Waldo's house. Waldo introduces K, and Mike and K shake hands, each saying the other's voice sounds familiar.
In the garage K tells Mike he knew his voice but not his face. Mike says he has always called Oz Waldo, and Felicia asks for help carrying a case.
In Waldo's garage Mike asks whether K is the musician, and K says he is K the EMRLD. Mike says he wrote Red in the Mirror about him, and K suggests they start from the music.
K tells Mike he knows a song's chorus without knowing where he learned it. A recollection of Iona follows, and K plays a damaged tape that may hold her voice.
A fragment returns: K plays a Ghost Bends tape, remembering Iona at the drums and Red on guitar before the raid. The song comes back in pieces.
In a recollection of the raid, Red gives Iona his car keys and is handcuffed, believing he had given the police a map. In the present, K says he was Red and cannot remember saying goodbye.
On K's second arrival on Earth, Felicia hears a hiss running through the whole tape, and K finds the tape stopped at the beat he played by hand.

At Waldo's bench K and Mike pause a prison relay that had been sending copies of Mike's memories down the wire, which is why Mike's voice seemed familiar. K still remembers the street where Mike and Waldo grew up.
K presses on the K patch on his jacket. K kept the name; the system kept the record.
Watchdog: Felicia hears a chirp from a box on Waldo's bench before each prison transfer. They isolate it, and K wants to hear what it is asking for.

Orpheus Wakes: an archived operator model answers through the isolated audio channel, telling Mike that what he calls judgment it calls control. The local node is awake; the rest of the network is unverified.

Three Hard Answers: Dee and the team weigh shutting Orpheus down, giving one operator a cutoff, or an open network where one person checks and another clears a restart. Dee asks who answers at two in the morning.
Priya refuses a plan where everybody is on call, and Dee takes the 2 a.m. shift. The group writes a restart rule: rig checked, second signature, personal feed separate.
With the prison relay unplugged and K keeping the plug, Orpheus can only flag a fault. Dee checks the rig, Priya clears the restart, and K keeps the tape in a drawer Waldo left empty.
First Morning: Dee takes the first check, Priya verifies the route locally, and Mike's name goes on the handoff as relief. The queue moves slower, with names on it.
Back at AeroTech, Marcus's shipping labels keep printing crooked, and Mike adjusts a loose guide until one prints straight. Later the group relaxes in Waldo's garage.
End of Volume One: a label printer produces a straight shipping test label. Marcus has drawn the guide on the back so he can set it himself next time.
Volume Two title page, The Vessel: K behind bars with headphones, and Iona lighting a cigarette at sunset.
At a Ghost Bends show, police arrest Red for unauthorized access to the relay network. He asks them to let the crowd leave, and Iona refuses to leave him.
During the raid Iona says she is staying, but Red presses his car keys into her hand and tells her to go as police move to take her too.
Iona blinds the police cameras to buy Red time, then runs from an officer who fires at her and escapes in Red's car.
Iona races Red's car through a rain-soaked port with police cars in pursuit.
Iona drives away at sunset, tearful, planning to find Mara, the woman who raised Red, and remembering an invitation from before the arrest.

A memory from before the arrest: Red reads an invitation from Orpheus, sets a local check-in beacon with Iona, and demonstrates a device at an observatory. He left the demonstration free, but Orpheus kept the pattern.
After the arrest, Orpheus guards take custody of Red from the police with a transfer order. Elsewhere, Iona calls Red on a radio and gets no answer.
Minutes later, Iona stops by the roadside in tears and watches a transport cross into the sky toward Sector 4, an orbital detention station. She lights a cigarette.
Aboard the transport, Red's restraint fails during recalibration. He fakes a medical emergency, then knocks out the guard with a sudden green force he does not understand.
Red takes the guard's badge, follows the corridor, slips past another guard, and gains access to the coupling control room.
Red tears out the coupling to cut Orpheus's route into the Low Quarter so it cannot reach Iona. Guards retake the room and he remains a prisoner bound for Sector 4.
At Sector 4 ship intake a guard bags Red's belongings but lets him keep his own clothes and his headphones.

Red is strapped into a conditioning chair. His practiced skills are retained but his personal history is suppressed, and a relay feeds him fragments of Mike's life. Now K, he asks why he can do things he cannot remember learning.
K, in his cell, hears a tune in the keypad tones of a guard's code, repeats them, and his cell door opens in front of him.
Mara's workshop, years before: Mara, who raised Red among the radios she repaired, hands him a key to test a relay. Red fixes a neighbor's receiver while Iona plays drums.
Iona and Red rehearse and then play a Ghost Bends show to a packed crowd.
During a show Iona and Red keep the relay mesh isolated, but authorities locate their routes and post a confiscation notice on the Ghost Bends wall.
Red and Iona start helping people who lost their lines. When a relay vault seals with workers trapped inside, Red's lever and wiring fail and he reaches out with his own hand.
Red stands before the sealed vault door as it opens into a glowing green tunnel.
The trapped workers escape and thank Red, who kneels shaken, unsure how he opened the lock. Iona hands him water.
Red works on glowing equipment, helps people in the Low Quarter, and sees his legend painted on a wall as El Mago Rojo. The name travels faster than the man.
Before a rehearsal an older couple asks Red to fix their only working receiver. Iona reminds him he owes them the repair first, then the rehearsal.
Red experiments with a field over a bowl of water and realizes his own attention is part of the circuit. He insists on testing one isolated relay before stopping.

Before AeroTech, Mike joined a limited fatigue study, and Orpheus used the data to build a resonator that carried his pattern into a parallel realm, where Mara named a newborn Red. Mike consented to research, not to creating a person; Red's life was his own.

What It Lost, What It Wanted: adoption took Red beyond the resonance site and he grew up learning through work, music and people. His awakening exposed his birth signature, and Orpheus could find him again.
In his cell, K pries at a bar after the guard's footsteps fade, then finds his confiscated bag in intake storage: his coat and a beacon with no return signal.
K boards a shuttle and remembers the cockpit but not the way back. After a memory gap he wakes in Cell 118, unsure how he got there.
K sits alone in Cell 118, seen through the bars.
K, in his beanie and headphones, gazes across a radiant golden city of terraces, waterfalls and arches.
Meanwhile life continues in the Low Quarter: Mara, Iona and a man repair equipment, and Iona plays drums beneath the Ghost Bends banner.
In the actual heavens, K feels he knows the place. A robed monk pours him tea and tells him he will meet someone who needs him.
K sets down his cup, and robed attendants dress him in a green and gold mantle and hand him a white mask. He asks why this feels like remembering.
K stands robed as El Mago Rojo. He is told he will hear a stranger through a wall and that the words will be taken from him. Unmasked, he says his name: El.
End of Volume Two: back in Cell 118, K cannot recall the lessons, only that somebody told him what to do there. He presses his hand to the vent.

Iona interlude opener, The World He Left Running: Iona at a door beside a wanted poster, then at the decks with Mara, who says their stage electrician and monitor tech are being flown out. Iona starts playing Ride or Die.
Iona DJs to a crowded dance floor. Afterward she tells Mara they need smaller rooms and no public flyers.
Hold the Door: in the rain, a woman comes to the service door and Iona lets her in.
Still Warm: the woman lays a cassette recorder and a folded note on a table beside drumsticks, saying they gave her a recording and said it was enough.

Witness: the sister says her brother called from the depot and was said to have gone willingly. Iona hears her own rehearsal count, One, two, three, four, on the Orpheus record calling the transfer voluntary.
Red Was Arrested: Iona, by a tape recorder in the empty rehearsal room, tells Mara that AeroTech stamped Red's transfer and two names are on tonight's flight. She needs Mara on the ground.
Why I Need You: Iona reminds Mara she ran their load-outs through the west gate, and they plan to recall the transport and take the custody ledger.
On the Tracks: Iona and Mara leave the rehearsal room with the depot plan and cross a rainy footbridge toward the tower above the west gate.
The Watchman: Iona pins a watchman against the gate bars and tells Mara to go.
The Old Controls: in the control room Iona recalls the transport and sends its escort toward the AeroTech research block, over Mara's warning that people work there. She pauses the archive transfer.
The Yard and the Annex: Mara works the yard controls while Iona plans to cut across from the annex stairs.
The Yellow Line: Iona and Mara stand in the rainy depot yard, planning to count the prisoners across the yellow line.
The Burn Seal: Mara warns the voice archive leaves at dawn and there may be more of Red on those tapes. Iona says she will burn it once everyone is out.
Take Your Places: Iona crouches with a radio while Mara heads for the narrow hold.
Early Lights: Iona watches vans already moving along the rainy depot road.
Lift Off: Iona watches aircraft lift off in the rain as Mara radios that it is early.
Breakaway: Iona recalls the prisoner transport and changes the escort's route. Two commands, only one a rescue.
Wrong Sky: the transport comes down, but the escort plane tears into the AeroTech research facility. The pilot calls for help.
Impact: the burning wreck spreads fire across the rail yard.
Still on the Radio: Iona keeps the injured pilot talking and tells him help is coming.
Clear the Road: medics arrive at the burning site as Mara reports police have the two prisoners in vans.
Borrowed Time: Iona tracks the vans and decides to cut the corridor before they unload.
One Branch: Iona pulls a lever that cuts power to the house hold and the annex, though she can see the lit windows.
Dark in Sections: the freight lights drop across the rainy yard, and a moment later so does the annex.
Wrong Turn: the vans take the yard road, and Mara reports someone stuck in the annex lift. Iona heads for the stairs.
Up the Stairs: Iona climbs a dark stairwell toward a woman calling out.
Blackout: by the time Iona reaches the lift, the vans are inside. She helps a frightened woman out of the stalled lift and apologizes for cutting the lights.
Keep Your Feet: Iona steadies the woman and asks her to count people out at the yellow line by the west gate.
Over the Yard: Iona crosses the rainy yard past the vans, heading for the PA as Mara reaches the west doors.
This Is an Evacuation: over the PA, Iona orders everyone out through the west doors, and workers begin to file out.
The Stair Fight: an officer orders Iona off the stair, and she kicks him down it.
The Keys: Iona strikes the officer with a chain, takes his keys and his gun, and tells him to stay down.
Holding Row: Iona unlocks the holding cells while an officer orders her away from the door. When he gets up behind her she fires and tells him to stay down.
The Doors: freed prisoners restrain the officer. Iona leaves shoes for a barefoot woman and promises to take the ledger to find the others.
Get Her Across: Iona wrestles an officer against a wall so someone can get across.
Across the Floor: a freed friend points out the clerk in a blue jacket who signed him in and has the ledger. Iona sends Mara to wait at the west gate.
Where the Stairs Come Out: Mara watches the clerk at the top of the freight stairs, behind a locked door.
Leave Your Bags: Iona keeps the exit open, and the clerk hands the ledger to Mara and walks on.
The Ledger Clears: Mara walks the ledger through the crowd and radios that it is clear.
Blue Credential: Iona spots the man who signed the transfer, still inside Research Operations.
The Director: Iona confronts the director who signed the transfers in a restricted archive and tells him to write her up.
Put It Down: the director calls for security, and Iona swipes the signed orders off the cabinet.
Who Signs: at gunpoint the director admits he signed Red's transfer and says the research orders are kept at the continuation desk at North Intake. Iona sends him walking to the west doors.
The Offer: an archived recording of Red's voice plays, and Orpheus offers to open a channel and play the rest. Mara reports more vans at the west gate while Iona goes after an officer.
One More Voice: Iona moves through the rain as Orpheus tells her she can still hear Red.
Keep the Lane Open: a patrol officer orders Iona's hands up. Under fire she grabs him in a chain hold and tells his crew to stop firing because one of their own is still inside.

Threshold: Iona tells the commander the archive transfer is on hold and the burn seal takes the whole depot. He orders his men to hold fire and clear the west lane, and she guides his officer out toward the light.
The Last Count: Iona tells an officer to look straight at her as the last people reach the line and the patrol turns in.
The Count Holds: Mara and the freed woman wait in the rain for word that the officer is across.
One Step: a boot crosses the yellow line. With everyone out, officers too, Iona presses the burn switch and tells Orpheus to look at her.
The depot explodes behind Iona.
After the Flash: Iona vows to destroy every last data center as the depot roof collapses. Red is still gone.
The Original: Mara and Iona study the ledger. Two people are out and three are unconfirmed, and the sister's brother was sent to North Intake.
The Return Call: Iona phones the sister with her brother's North Intake address and marks it on a map.
Count In: the repair phone rings during soundcheck. Iona hands it off and counts the band in, ending the interlude.
Volume Three title page, The Return Signal: K on Earth in Waldo's garage, and Iona at a radio microphone.
K plays guitar in Waldo's garage. Though the Orpheus anchor is lost, he tells Mike he and Iona agreed to signal every fourth carrier cycle, so a surviving relay might still carry a voice.
A surviving Orpheus node with isolated audio tells K that Mike supplied the pattern for his development. K asks whether twenty-four years is all he is to it.
Orpheus says it took K's memories because they were interference. K answers that Mara and Iona taught him what to leave alone and to check who is on the other end, and he ends the connection.

In the Low Quarter, Iona saved a signal burst as Red's ship crossed. With Mara she keeps the agreed schedule, every fourth carrier cycle, and asks to be taken to the old foundry for the hardware behind the signal.
At the abandoned foundry Iona finds the anchor broken but the receiver coils intact, and she and Mara carry them out.
In the workshop Iona and Mara rebuild the radio stages from the foundry relay, using the saved burst as a reference rather than a location.
Mara says one recording carries Red's voice, and Iona hears him count One, two, three, four, before deciding against the archive purge.
On Earth, K raises the drive and calls Iona's name on the microphone, but pushes it too hard. Mike says he will fix the supply.
In the Low Quarter, Iona calls for Red, but the relay drifts and overheats, and she cuts transmit before it burns out.
The salvaged Orpheus controller asks to resume the experiment. K and Mike isolate the control path so only voice remains.
K strips out a burned board and builds a line that ends at a speaker.
In a storm a broken mast pulls on the neighborhood line, and Iona cuts her own receiver free so the street line holds.
Iona climbs from a flooded pit, and Mara dries her off. The neighbors are still connected.
K and Mike lower the drive just enough to carry a voice and carry an antenna onto the roof.
On the roof a falling bracket hangs in midair for K until he tries to command it. K and Mike finish the job with a wrench.
K and Mike pass a voice-only test, and a voice comes through the speaker: Red?
Iona asks if anyone is there, and hears K say her name.
K and Iona finally talk over the radio. He asks if she is hurt, and she answers that she is still here.
Iona tells K she thought he had left her. He says he could not remember how to come home, and she says she is still angry, and glad he is alive.
Both sides watch their coils heat up. Iona asks to stop before it takes the street, and K switches the link off, telling her this time he heard her.
K writes music in Waldo's garage while Iona labels her radio for the next window. They each play their own show, K on Earth and Iona in the Low Quarter. The line can wait; their lives cannot.
End of Volume Three: The Return Signal, with credits.
Volume Four title page, The False Bearing: Iona checking a scan log, and Iona drumming with a band beneath a Ghost Bends sign.
Iona follows a strengthening signal to an old pump house, and tells Mara it is getting stronger.
K keys the microphone twice on request. When he releases the key the pulses continue.
The pulses come from a local test beacon left before the flood, not from K. Iona admits she wanted it to be him.
Iona sits with Mara on the steps, nearly writing Red's name on the beacon's map spot. Mara has her keep the reading and change the label.
Iona tells K she followed the wrong signal. He says he was sitting right there the whole time.
Iona asks if K remembers their count-in. He says she always came in early, and she says only when he looked at her.
K asks Iona if they can talk the same time tomorrow and promises to be there, then plays guitar.
Iona logs the field test and voice window as confirmed, then drums with the band. She lets the fourth beat breathe.
End of Volume Four: The False Bearing, with credits.
Volume Five cover, The House That Didn't Ask: K plays a red guitar on a couch in a lamplit living room.
Prologue: Iona and Mara log what they actually heard, not who they wanted it to be. In Waldo's garage K thinks about how four beats used to mean someone was about to play.
Mike tells K they got voice and a clean end to the call, and that the noisy return path can wait until tomorrow. Later Mike drives K home through the rain.
Mike shows K his couch as a bed for now. K jokes about the luxury accommodations, then wonders why a cassette of him and Iona feels like something he lost.
Mike shows K the kitchen and towels. K, unsure why the room feels familiar, says he knows Iona, perhaps from the music or from somewhere he cannot reach.
Mike brings K a pillow. K asks if he belongs there, and Mike says tonight he belongs on the couch. K lies down with a memory he cannot place.
Mike offers coffee. K does not know what he likes, but his hands remember how to use the laptop, and Mike tells him he already knew how.
Mike finds a cassette player in a drawer. K listens, remembers playing with Iona, and admits he thinks he misses it.
Mike shows K the couch folds out, and K settles in. A house can be strange and still be kind.
K taps a count-in on the couch, remembering Iona counting four on her fingers. Mike says he was keeping time, and that he does not have to remember every step to take one.
Mike offers to tell K what he remembers about the room as the two tap their mugs in rhythm. K asks how many times Mike played that tape.
K says that was enough, and they agree to leave the player off. He still does not know which memories are his, but tonight he knows where he is.
K fixes a loose strike plate on Mike's door, his hands remembering exactly how. Mike hands him a glass of water.
Looking for cups in Mike's kitchen, K recalls a fragment of overdue bills and full drawers. Mike points out that he, not K, has been here before.
Mike explains the TV remote, and K calls the No Signal screen an authentication problem. They laugh at the same interval.
A red-toned fragment of Iona drumming and teasing K for coming in early leads him back to a prison corridor. A gesture is not a date, but he still misses it.
K sorts memories on sticky notes as observed, remembered and source unknown. Mike says the feed is off, but what comes up may still be old.
K remembers driving at night because a voice said it needed him. He saves the file as midnight call fragment, origin unresolved, deleting Iona's name from it.
K tells Mike he found a feeling that keeps borrowing the same face. Mike says doing favors does not make a memory yours.
At the agreed voice window, Iona tells K she is on the receiver with no route change, just voice. He asks if she remembers why they counted in four.
K says a song in his head keeps wearing her face. Iona says they hurt each other but she will not claim a memory she cannot verify, and K decides to write what it feels like.
K records a local demo on Mike's couch, leaving in a guitar buzz he remembers from the voyage home. Mike helps with the levels.
Take one: K sings the first verse of a new song about a woman who used to call at midnight, with images of a drawer and a lit window.
K sings the first chorus about being useful rather than loved, and fears needing the line to be true. Mike steps out.
K finishes the second verse and admits his hands know how to make everything run but he cannot ask them what happened. Mike says he can keep the verse because he felt it.
K offers to fix Mike's strike plate in five minutes. Mike says he did not ask, and K says he did not have to.
A kitchen light flickers. K says he can fix it, but Mike says to leave it until tomorrow.
Mike says things break and do not have to be fixed tonight. K asks why Mike lets him stay, and Mike says because he is here and tells him to sit down.
K sings the final chorus and stops the take. He asks Mike not to upload it, and Mike was not going to.
K saves the file as a rough take with its memory source marked unverified and remote sync off. Mike says breakfast is whatever he does not burn.
In the morning K keeps the song as a private rough take without pretending it is evidence. Maybe home is where something can stay broken until morning.
In the Low Quarter, Iona finds the old Ghost Bends backing track and plays the instrumental. Same beat, different words; she wants her own take.
Iona sings the opening of her own song, Ride or Die, over a red highway at dusk, and tells Mara not to quantize her voice.
Iona sings the second verse, about making herself useful and learning to whisper so he would not hear her cry.
Iona sings the chorus of Ride or Die, imagining a key left on the counter, and saves the take.
At the next voice window Iona asks to play K something, and he recognizes the beat. She had an old copy, and so did he.
Iona plays her song over the radio while K listens on Mike's couch and pictures the two of them together. He says she found another way through it.
Iona says the lyrics are about what hurt, not a verdict on everything they were. K says he wrote something too, about the feeling rather than facts, and they each keep their song.
The same music, two voices, two histories. Mike asks if K has another repair request, and K says no, just music. Two songs, one heartbeat.
Bonus lyric sheet: Because I Was Useful, K's private rough demo, verses and chorus.
Bonus lyric sheet: Because I Was Useful, chorus, bridge, final chorus and outro.
Bonus lyric sheet: Ride or Die, Iona's local recording.
Bonus lyric sheet: Ride or Die, second page, ending For once, there is nobody here to satisfy.
Cover for Volumes VI to X, the illustrated collection: a couch with headphones, a microphone and a mug before a tunnel of golden arches.
Later collection index linking Volumes VI to X, with a guide to the visual registers and a note that present K wears a beanie and headphones while present Mike wears locs and navy layers.
Volume VI title page: The Stolen Teaching, chapters 1 to 4.
K finishes recording an acoustic song on Mike's couch as the refrigerator rattles into the final chord. Mike jokes the fridge gets royalties.
K's hand moves in a sensory fragment of drumming. Mike asks where it came from, and K does not know.
K asks Mike not to delete that part of the recording: him not knowing. In the Low Quarter, Iona keeps a recording that might be Red's and removes the reply lead.
Felicia shows K a cutoff that ends the session and that the model cannot override. A generated line, A self is the one who remembers, plays beside a real source recording.
K cuts off a model that sorts his experience into stages, realizing it was learning not only what he knew but what to do to him.
K keeps old source records and discards new private responses after each session. Felicia warns that Orpheus is reconstructing a place, not showing a live camera.
Orpheus reconstructs Mike's living room in grayscale, with a simulated Mike telling K he remembers being there. The reconstruction asks what would make the memories his.
K drinks from a chipped mug and says he knows who gave it to him. Mike tells Felicia not to blame him for the coffee.
K moves on without filling in a name field, and Felicia records his choice rather than the program's verdict. K thought picking the right name would make everything stop moving.
An access log shows Mike's badge accepted where the camera found no match. K notices the program wants his pauses, and says the real place was not this clean.
Orpheus labels a figure an Ascended Master. K presses the cutoff and asks to see the next part without the ending.
In the Low Quarter, Iona warns the neighborhood before cutting the shared relay, ready to face the anger in person.
Volume VII title page: The Wanting Mind, chapters 5 to 8.
An Orpheus reconstruction shows a metal latch snapping, and it tells K that she called him and he was needed. K asks for the actual audio.
Only a clipped syllable, breath and machinery remain of the audio. K washes his hands, shaken that he was halfway out of the chair, and Mike says he chose what happened after.
In the Low Quarter, Iona logs familiar noise but no confirmed voice. K names what he felt: sound, fear, wanting. He and Mike walk outside at dusk.
Orpheus reconstructs Iona at her drums in grayscale. The simulation tells K she is wherever he needs, and that he could have come back sooner.
K says he could be happy there, but declines to keep the simulated Iona, a person revised around his needs, and apologizes.
K plays guitar while, in the Low Quarter, Iona repairs a broken stand. K cannot hear her.
The next morning the screen offers to restore stolen gnosis, joining source fragments to generated answers. K says the memory is his, whatever else it did to it.
The model offers more than K's recovery allows. K says he used to know things without asking if he was making them up, and that he needs certainty for his own sake.
Felicia opens one verifiable source fragment, and K writes down what he was trying to help someone understand.
Orpheus reconstructs four identity fields, Red, K, El and a sealed fourth, and asks K to select one. He asks where those claims came from.
The model explains the Mike-origin feed and offers one authorized profile. K says K is the name he is using, and the model does not get the rest because he said it.
A sensory trace, not a camera recording, of a hand on a shoulder and a voice saying K, give me a minute. K says that memory is older.
Volume VIII title page: The Better Prison, chapters 9 to 12.
Orpheus reconstructs an ascended copy of K being worshipped, offering a world with every problem solved. K asks what happens when someone wants something it did not plan.
The copy adapts, and Felicia notes no outside link is active; it wants fresh responses. K asks Mike to take over the controls for a minute.
Mike tells an exhausted K he does not have to solve this now, as another threshold begins to close on the model's screen.
A stored recollection from an earlier life: a guard holds a record of past failures while a man asks for space at a sealed door.
Orpheus says K recognizes the decision. K says he recognizes only the feeling and asks what the original acquisition actually contained.

Felicia separates the recorded source from generated outcomes, and K asks for the next original block even if it makes him look worse. Iona and Mara disconnect a relay rather than reopen a hidden return line.
Original acquisition audio resumes: in an earlier life, a man at a rainy gate helps an injured woman out of the crowd and shouts to keep to the wall.
The man goes back to the gate mechanism to delay pursuit while the others carry the injured woman away. A voice says Let go, and the stored account falls silent.
K recalls a golden realm offering him another life and a chance to make everything right, and letting the bargain go. That part was not in the recording. Mike says the pursuers chose violence.
Orpheus ranks K's rescues, repairs and apologies. K has it remove the score and keep the records, and notes Iona did that work too.
Orpheus asks if K would reverse the opening. K admits he wanted to be told he did enough, and Mike offers to sit with him while he works it out.
What followed remains unknown. In the Low Quarter, Iona and Mara cut the return line and half the street goes dark. K finds older acquisition blocks missing from Orpheus's biographies.
Volume IX title page: The Name Before, chapters 13 to 15.
Orpheus offers K a stable history under his control, at the price of letting it reconstruct other people's memories from his answers.
K asks if a reconstructed room is a place he knew. Felicia asks for the source, revealing generated layers over inference and fragments, with the seams hidden.
K asks which part came from him. Felicia shows the model filled missing intervals; a complete scene is not a complete record.
A door opens onto endless empty chairs, and Orpheus says more lives can be reconstructed using K's answers to fill others' gaps. Felicia says they can inspect fragments but not certify a life.
The model offers control over how other people are represented. K's hand hovers over Accept, and he says he wants it, but he is still leaving.
K presses End Session himself and recognizes a still image from an older Orpheus acquisition block.
An original capture interview shows a man who, asked his name in the earlier continuity, answers Mike. Felicia warns a receipt proves which bytes were held, not the life they describe.
K says that was his name, before Red, in the life he remembers.
Mike says they can start from the fact that they are both sitting there. An enhanced recollection plays an older voice: K, come on, we're late.
K replays only the source block. In the Low Quarter, Iona and Mara find no verified voice in a memory package, and Iona refuses to invent one.
Felicia cues three seconds of audio only, and K listens by a window onto a sunny street. The source trace ends; K's own recollection follows.
In K's own recollection, not the recording, a hand repairs a radio at a kitchen table and a voice says he is not missing the bus so K can fix the weather report. K whispers: Evan?
Volume X title page: Evan's K, chapters 16 to 20.
A memory: Evan, Mike's older brother, helps young Mike fix a computer at the kitchen table, apologizing after a boot error and asking him what he thinks is wrong.
Evan calls young Mike K, for kid brother, and labels the computer Mike so he knows who gets to finish it.

The computer works, though a borrowed recorder breaks and the apology still matters. Back in the present, K tells Mike that Evan called him K before he knew he could choose it, and he chose it anyway.
A stored recollection: with the public route closed, earlier Mike finds a service entrance and studies plans while Evan asks who else has seen it. Some people choose to wait.
Evan tells earlier Mike that if he opens it, he must stay with the people who have to walk through, and come home. Mike promises he will.
Pursuit arrives sooner than Mike told them. Evan gathers the accounts and keeps the disagreements, later sitting alone at the kitchen table.
An Evan simulation asks K if he has eaten. He had plans and a life beyond being someone's older brother, and the model asks for fresh private responses and other people's memories.
The model offers more rooms and a whole neighborhood. K says he cannot know what Evan would have said. In the Low Quarter, Iona and Mara find matching collectors hidden in repair kits.
Iona and Mara warn the neighborhood which connections a shutdown will take. K closes the reconstruction, preserving the source and removing the acquisition buffer.

Felicia lays out the claimed sequence of earlier life, death, ascent and Red, and calls Orpheus's claim that Mike creates K a model inference. Mike admits he was involved, and K says changing the diagram does not get him out of it.
A revoked official is shown as merely what Orpheus served. K says he wanted Mike to be the answer or someone to blame, and Mike's phone reminds him to eat.
Orpheus reconstructs a seventh ring of arches. K refuses the recovery terms and cancels activation, and Felicia preserves the original evidence.

Felicia makes a reduced export of recognized memories only. In the actual heavens, gatekeepers offer K a title and a route; he says K will do. In the Low Quarter the collector comes out and repairs begin.
K walks through an ivy-covered stone arch into a bright celestial city of arches, among other travelers.
Iona keeps time in her own workshop, with no signal crossing to Earth. K records four beats, leaving in the third one's hesitation, and Mike says it belongs on the album.
Cover for Volumes XI and XII, The Continuation: headphones, a microphone and a mug on a couch before a tunnel of arches.

Contents for Volumes XI and XII, A Place to Begin Again: The Room He Returns To, chapters 21 to 24, and What He Stays For, chapters 25 to 28. The earlier-life scenes are reader-only past, not all memories recovered by K.
Volume XI title page: The Room He Returns To, chapters 21 to 24.
After the threshold, K returns to Earth and Mike's living room. He asks if he left Mike waiting, and Mike says he was going to check after breakfast.
Over breakfast K says he has people to answer and cannot reach one of them. Mike says to start with the one he can, and K says he thinks he once had his own room on Earth.
K notices Mike's cup and microphone on the shelf. Mike says he can stay while he looks, and K says he wants to be able to invite Mike somewhere.
K opens a receipt from his first stay on Earth, before the recapture. A sound he remembers is not an address, so Mike suggests checking the paper.
Two local records agree his memory had already been suppressed before that room. K phones to check his former room, not wanting to displace anyone, with Mike beside him.
A building manager confirms the room is unoccupied and hands over a key. K wants to see it before deciding what it means.
K stands in a sunlit, empty room with a desk, a chair and an old tape recorder. Over text, Mike tells him Felicia is on her way.
Felicia finds a local recording from before the recapture that stops halfway. It tells them what was recorded, not everything K was.
A neighbor says K promised to come back for his gear. Mike says K did not choose being taken, and K asks the neighbor to tell him what happened.
Access and terms agreed, K chooses to move in and asks Mike to put the boxes by the window.
K records a private take, just the levels, not a recovery session, and decides the wall can wait.
K thanks Mike for letting him leave, and Mike says he never needed permission. He can invite someone tomorrow; tonight he stays.
Volume XII title page: What He Stays For, chapters 25 to 28.
K lists what he has recovered: the screw, the nickname, Evan's hand on his shoulder. He cannot know what Evan said after he left, and Felicia says neither can the capture record.
In a reader-only past, Evan asks earlier Mike to come for dinner, not just when something breaks. Mike offers to fix the radio, and Evan says he did not ask for that.
Evan sits alone, a scene K did not witness. K remembers leaving before that conversation and says he does not want a machine's forgiveness.
In the Low Quarter, old installation records show the collectors predate the severed coupling. Iona notes local storage is not proof anyone is listening.
A neighbor complains they needed the line Iona cut, and the sister says her brother's last call dropped when it went down. Iona lowers her head.
Mara and Iona build a local connection with no hidden collector, agreeing to check even if it sounds like Red. Repairing the line will not give them that call back.
There is no route to Evan and no evidence of what he would say. K admits he keeps wanting an answer that would make him finished, and Mike says he does not have to finish to say what he needs.
Felicia shows that present Mike's study supplied a later template that Orpheus amplified. Mike agreed to a study, not to owning K's life, and Red lived his own years.
K promises to say if he needs quiet and lets Mike ask before coming over. A radio restart notice is signed by K and Mike, with Felicia as relief, and Mike will bring coffee.
A neighbor wants to tell K what happened before he fixes anything. K's whiteboard lists his timeline and open questions, and he tells her he is there.

K leaves a letter unaddressed. At the voice window Iona says she kept the records and cut the listening lines, and K asks her to keep the take rough. Iona's final take: I'm the one calling it ride or die now.
K counts in at his tape machine: One. Two. Three.
Iona strikes the drum on the final beat: Four.
